source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Only 26 of Virginia's 332 mapped data centers publish a megawatt figure, so the 36 MW at NTT Ashburn VA7 is one of the few capacity numbers the state's power demand can be measured against.

The 36 MW ranks 14th among those 26 disclosing facilities and equals 2.2 percent of Virginia's published 1,639.4 MW. The building holds 125,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that capacity corresponds to roughly 900 racks and roughly 1,100 to 1,400 accelerators, depending on configuration. Those conversions are estimates derived from the published megawatt figure, not counts from the operator.

For AI specifically, the megawatt figure is the number that matters, because accelerator count follows power rather than floor area. Ashburn is where most of Virginia's published capacity concentrates, and this facility sits there. But nothing published says whether it carries AI workloads or what its grid connection is. The same 36 MW could serve training, inference, or ordinary enterprise computing.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. No certifications are published, and announced expansion is the one input missing from the suitability score of 68, which otherwise rests on published IT capacity and operator type. The state total of 1,639.4 MW sums only the facilities that disclose, so it is a floor rather than a census of Virginia data center load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
